title: Hardware affinity pools and burst-credit isolation for tenant throughput guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity are observing bursty tenants that transiently exhaust shared PCIe/BANDWIDTH or scheduler slots leading to head-of-line latency spikes for co-located tenants. Existing lane-quota heuristics reduce incidents but do not offer predictable short-term throughput guarantees or controlled burst capacity.

Goal: Implement a two-tier isolation mechanism that (1) assigns tenants to affinity pools with explicit hardware pinning to eliminate cross-pool interference for critical workloads, and (2) provides a burst-credit system per-tenant that affords controlled short-duration throughput above baseline without violating pool-level SLOs. The feature should be configurable per-reservation and enforceable by the scheduler/runtime with telemetry surfaced in Console.

Success criteria: predictable p99 token latency under normal and burst scenarios for tenants with affinity, bounded cross-tenant bandwidth contention, and ability for ops/solutions to set burst budgets and reclaim policies for noisy tenants.
motivation: Customers buying Dedicated expect both throughput guarantees and the ability to let occasional short bursts occur for traffic spikes. Hardware-level affinity minimizes shared resource noise (NVLink/PCIe/switch buffers) while burst credits let tenants temporarily oversubscribe without impacting pool SLAs. This reduces support load and churn for high-SLA customers.
proposed_solution: 1) Affinity pools: extend the scheduler to support named affinity pools mapped to node labels (e.g., "affinity:low-noise", "affinity:general") and support hard pinning of tenant reservations to a pool. 2) Burst-credit ledger: per-tenant token-based budget stored in control-plane (softly enforced by runtime). Credits decay over time (sliding window recharge). 3) Pool caps and emergency reclaim: each pool has a pool-level bandwidth cap and a reclaim policy that, when violated, throttles tenants by draining credit first then applying proportional slowdown. 4) Telemetry: per-tenant and per-pool counters emitted to metrics backend and Console surfaces (burst remaining, last reclaim event, pool utilization).
implementation_notes: - Scheduler changes: add affinity label evaluation at placement time and node set for reservation. - Runtime enforcement: augment per-request admission with credit check; if credits exhausted and pool under pressure, return early throttle (HTTP 429-like internal signal) or apply token rate limit. - Control plane: ledger persisted in Redis or internal strong-store with atomic decrement and TTL-based recharge transactions. - Config API: allow reservation creation to include affinity:pool and burst_policy {window_seconds:int, max_credits:int, recharge_rate:float}. - Backwards compatibility: default reservations map to existing 'general' pool with no burst budget. - Performance: credit checks must be sub-millisecond on hot path; consider batched RPCs or local caches with pessimistic invalidation for correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity pool pinning ensures 95th percentile inter-tenant bandwidth interference reduced by >= 80% in microbenchmarks compared to 'general' pool.
Burst credits allow short-term throughput bump up to configured max_credits and recharge behavior matches configured window across repeated spikes.
Under sustained overload, pool reclaim sequence prevents any single tenant from causing pool-level SLO violations (measured via synthetic multi-tenant load tests).
Console shows per-tenant burst budget, recent reclaim events, and per-pool utilization charts.
Docs updated with API examples and recommended affinity/burst configurations for common workloads.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger atomics and scheduler affinity matching, integration tests deploying multi-tenant clusters with synthetic traffic generators to simulate noisy behavior, e2e tests for Console telemetry and reclaim flows. Load tests to validate sub-ms credit checks under 10k req/s per node. Canary rollout to a single region with opt-in tenants before global rollout.
metrics_and_slo: - Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 token latency. - Pool-level throughput and bandwidth utilization. - Number of reclaim events per hour. - Percentage of requests served from burst budget vs baseline. Target: p99 latency for affinity tenants < 150ms under 90% pool utilization.
rollout_plan: 1) Migrate a small set of internal reservations to 'low-noise' affinity for validation (week 1). 2) Enable burst ledger in read-only telemetry mode for 2 weeks to observe recharge patterns. 3) Opt-in customers can enable burst credits + affinity (week 3). 4) Gradual ramp and enable automatic reclaim for opted pools (week 4). Monitor and rollback thresholds defined in runbook.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: ledger contention at high QPS could add latency. Mitigation: local caching with lease tokens and fallback to strong-store for debug. - Risk: misconfiguration may starve general pool. Mitigation: sane default budgets and pool caps with alerts. - Risk: enforcement adds overhead to hot path. Mitigation: microbench kernel to measure and optimize credit check path; inline fast-path for tenants with no burst enabled.
rollout_notes: Ops runbook added: commands to move a reservation between pools, to zero-out burst budgets for a tenant, and to diagnose reclaim causes. Monitor alerts: pool_utilization > 90% for 5m, reclaim_events > 10/min.
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on two-layer approach (hardware affinity + burst ledger). Action: Marcus to prototype ledger API.
2026-02-24: Prototype ledger stores credits in Redis using LUA script for atomicity. Initial microbench shows 150k ops/s. Follow-up: measure tail latency under churn.
2026-03-02: Design review feedback from PM (Rosa Gomez): add Console UX to visualize burst depletion and an explicit 'reclaim reason' in event payloads. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-07: Implemented scheduler affinity label matching and unit tests. PR opened: runtime#8912. Performance regression benchmark scheduled.
2026-03-10: Integration tests failing on rare race where local credit cache stale leads to over-issuance. Mitigation: reduce cache lease to 200ms and add compensating adjustment in ledger.
